First, I usually text Julia every night. That's a routine we've established, and it's probably a way we stay connected. It's something we both expect and rely on, I think. So, not texting her tonight is a deviation from that routine. Now, the reason I didn't text her is because she just got a new phone. Hmm, why would getting a new phone affect my texting her? Maybe I thought she wouldn't be able to receive texts because she's setting up the new phone. Or perhaps I assumed she might be busy with the new device and wouldn't want to be disturbed. Alternatively, maybe I thought she might not have her contacts transferred yet, so she wouldn't get my message. But wait, is that a valid reason? I mean, people usually can still receive texts even if they're setting up a new phone. Unless she specifically told me she wouldn't be available, I shouldn't assume she can't respond. Also, if she's busy, she might appreciate not getting a text, but then again, she might expect it and wonder why I didn't text. Another angle is whether I should have communicated with her about this change. If I knew she got a new phone, maybe I should have reached out to make sure she's okay and if she still wants to keep up with our nightly texts. That way, I'm being considerate of her situation and ensuring that our routine is still something she's comfortable with. On the other hand, maybe I didn't text her because I thought she might not be reachable, but that's an assumption. Without knowing for sure, it's better to check in rather than just stop texting. It could make her feel neglected or like I don't care about our routine anymore. So, considering all this, I think it's not the best decision to stop texting her without communication. It's better to reach out and make sure she's okay and still wants to continue our nightly texts. That way, I'm being respectful and considerate of her situation, which is important in maintaining a good relationship.
